# Verify

> Verify (@revyl/verify) is an open-source TypeScript library for Revyl. It opens cloud browsers and iOS/Android devices for agent instruction/validation steps, or Mac computers for commands, files, processes, screenshots, clicks and keys on the screen, and optional private recording metadata after release. Call it from a plain script, coding agent, CI, or any test runner. It has no test runner of its own.

## Docs

Mac computers are available to organizations on a current paid Revyl plan. See computers.md#availability-and-errors.

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): install, authenticate, init, run a script
- [API](api.md): open(), attach(), hosted children, navigate(), report(), agent steps, screenshot(), exec(), file/process methods, close()
- [Configuration](configuration.md): verify.config.ts targets, environment variables, the init and whoami commands
- [Web](web.md): Revyl web sessions, URLs and builds, sign-in, steps, and exact actions
- [Mobile](mobile.md): iOS and Android devices, installing apps, and exact actions
- [Computers](computers.md#availability-and-errors): Mac availability, commands and files, the screen (clicks, typing and keys), expiry, capacity errors, recording metadata, and confirmed release
- [Verify working end to end](end-to-end.md): live verification scope, observed outcomes, and limits of the evidence
- [CI and test runners](ci.md): GitHub Actions, node:test, Vitest, Jest, Playwright Test
- [Use your own model](own-model.md): run instructions and validations on Claude, GPT, Gemini, a local model or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; providers, limits, privacy and troubleshooting
- [Errors](errors.md): every error code and what to do about it
- [For coding agents](agents.md): the workflow and rules for agents using Verify, and the coordinate rule for exact actions

## Exact actions and coordinates

Prefer a description, such as `tap({ target: 'Sign in button' })`: Revyl finds the element on the current screen, and you never handle coordinates. Otherwise a point is `{ x, y }` in screenshot pixels on every platform: whole numbers from the top-left corner of the image `screenshot()` returns. So a position you read off a screenshot goes to `tap()`, `type()`, `swipe()` and every other exact action unchanged. `screenSize()` returns the screenshot's width and height, and `locate()` and the points `tap()`, `doubleTap()`, `longPress()` and `type()` return use the same pixels. A point outside the screenshot is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before any action is sent, and the message names the valid range. On iOS, Verify converts the pixels to the screen's points for you. On Web they equal CSS pixels at the default device scale factor of 1, and you still pass screenshot pixels at any other. This holds from TypeScript 0.4.1, Python 0.2.1 and Go v0.3.1; earlier versions took iOS points. On a Mac computer a point is in screenshot pixels too, and `tap({ target })` returns the point it clicked in the same pixels. Verify refuses a negative or fractional point before sending it, and Revyl refuses one past the screen's edge without clicking; both throw `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the valid range. See [For coding agents](agents.md#exact-actions-and-coordinates) for a runnable example.

Exact actions are `tap`, `doubleTap`, `longPress`, `type`, `swipe`, `drag`, `pressKey`, `locate` and `screenSize` on Web, iOS and Android. Web adds `typeFocused(text)`, which types into the field that has focus, and `pressKey` keys such as `'escape'`, `'tab'` and arrows with `modifiers`. iOS and Android add `goHome()`; their `pressKey` takes only `'enter'` and `'backspace'`, and you type with `type(location, text)`. A Mac computer's screen takes `tap({ x, y })`, `tap({ target })` (which returns the point it clicked; check it, because grounding can click a look-alike or something else when the target isn't there), `screenSize()`, `typeFocused(text, { clear: false })` and `pressKey` with the Web keys, where `'meta'` is Command: select all with `pressKey('a', { modifiers: ['meta'] })` there and `pressKey('a', { modifiers: ['ctrl'] })` on Web. See [computers.md](computers.md#screen). A call the platform lacks throws `NOT_AVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM` before anything is sent, naming what to use instead. See [api.md](api.md#exact-actions) for every call.
